title: SDK Micro-Feedback Loop & Telemetry Proposal (draft)
content:
Summary:

This note outlines a lightweight, privacy-first micro-feedback loop and telemetry plan for Redwood SDKs. The goal is to capture high-signal telemetry around first-touch and early adoption flows so we can iterate on DX, reduce time-to-first-success, and detect regressions in the starter experience without shipping heavy instrumentation for every surface.

Goals:
- Quickly measure first-10-minutes success for a new SDK user (signup -> first request -> basic success).
- Surface friction points (auth errors, missing config, confusing error messages).
- Collect anonymized user feedback prompts at critical moments (first successful call, repeated failures).
- Keep telemetry minimal, sampled, and easy to opt-out of.
- Provide actionable dashboards and a small set of alerts for regressions and spikes.

Design principles:
- Minimal: keep the event surface small (10-12 event types max).
- Privacy-first: no PII, no request/response payloads, only metadata and error classes.
- Low-latency: events should be emitted asynchronously and not block SDK usage.
- Configurable: allow customers to opt out or change sampling rates via environment variables or agent config.
- Backwards-compatible: add new events in a non-breaking way.

Priority event set (proposed):
1. sdk.installed           - when SDK is installed (local telemetry, only if opt-in)
2. sdk.configured          - when API key or connection config is set
3. sdk.first_request       - first outbound API call attempt
4. sdk.first_success       - first successful response (2xx where applicable)
5. sdk.first_error         - first error response (class: auth/network/usage/timeout/parse)
6. sdk.retry_attempt       - automatic retry occurred
7. sdk.fallback_invoked    - fallback model/route used due to capacity/error
8. sdk.cli-stub-run        - local simulation or cli quickstart executed
9. sdk.opt_in_feedback     - user opted in to give short feedback after first success
10. sdk.feature_flag       - capture major feature/seed config (e.g., local-mode=true)

For each event record the following minimal attributes (no PII):
- sdk_version (string)
- platform (python/node/go)
- os_family (mac/windows/linux)
- install_channel (pip/npm/apt/manual) when applicable
- error_class (auth/network/timeout/parse/other) for errors
- latency_ms (for success/error events)
- sample_rate (the effective sampling fraction)
- region_hint (if customer is on Redwood Dedicated/Private)
- trace_id (random UUID per session for grouping, not tied to user identity)

Event examples (text lines to copy into implementation):
- sdk.first_request {sdk_version: "0.13.2", platform: "python", os_family: "linux", install_channel: "pip", sample_rate: 0.05, trace_id: "b2b9..."}
- sdk.first_error {sdk_version: "0.13.2", platform: "python", error_class: "auth", latency_ms: 120, sample_rate: 0.05}

Sampling & privacy decisions:
- Default sampling: 5% for all install/config events, 20% for first_success/first_error to ensure enough signal for failure analysis. Allow env override: REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=0.01
- Never capture request/response text, prompt tokens, or user-provided data.
- Use a session-level trace_id that rotates after 24 hours; store in ephemeral local cache only.
- If running in Private/VPC mode, default to disabled and surface an explicit opt-in API for telemetry to the tenant admin.

Opt-in UX and lightweight feedback prompt:
- After sdk.first_success (only if sample allows), show a single, non-blocking prompt in the cli or library logs: "If this helped, please press Y to share an anonymous thumbs-up and a 1-line note. Opt out with REDWOOD_SDK_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1."
- Store feedback as a short 140-char string or a bucketed tag ("worked","confusing","auth-issue").

Implementation plan & timeline (6 weeks MVP):
Week 1: finalize event set and attributes, get legal signoff on privacy brief.
Week 2: implement async telemetry client (server endpoint + stub) and add sdk.first_request/first_success/first_error in python SDK.
Week 3: mirror node + go SDKs with same schema; add env flags and sampling config.
Week 4: add CLI lightweight prompt flow and opt-in capture; add unit tests and instrumentation toggles.
Week 5: deploy collection pipeline to internal analytics sandbox, build initial dashboards (first-success rate, top error classes, time-to-first-success CDF).
Week 6: run a 2-week canary with 1% of new signups, iterate on schema, prepare roll-out doc.

Dashboards & alerts (initial):
- KPI 1: Time-to-first-success median and P90 by SDK and platform.
- KPI 2: First-success rate (percent of sessions that get a success within 10 minutes of first request).
- KPI 3: Top 5 error_class by frequency.
- Alert: drop in first-success rate > 10% week-over-week for any platform.
- Alert: sudden spike in fallback_invoked events (>3x baseline).

Rollout considerations for Hosted / Dedicated / Private:
- Hosted: default opt-in with sampling. Provide dashboard access in Redwood Console under "DevX SDK Signals".
- Dedicated: default disabled; customers can enable with a tenant-level toggle and set sample rates.
- Private/on-prem: telemetry disabled by default. Offer an on-prem collector with metrics-only mode (no network outbound) that writes to a local telemetry sink (customer-managed).

Backwards/forwards compatibility notes:
- Use flexible key-value attributes; consumers must tolerate unknown keys.
- Version the event schema with event_schema_version attribute. Older SDK versions that lack fields should still emit core fields.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should sampling be for small customers to ensure signal? Proposal: bias sampling to prefer SDK runs that hit a new org id (if present) but never use PII.
- Do we want to capture model_id or model class? Helps routing/fallback analysis but may leak internal model choices; propose hashed model family (md5 truncated) as a compromise.
- Do we route some error telemetry to support for immediate customer help? If yes, need consent and clear opt-in.

Next steps:
- Owners: assign implementation leads for python/node/go SDKs and infra tracking (Raj for python, Emily for node, Leo for infra).
- Legal: produce 1-page privacy brief and checklist (target EOD week 1).
- Instrumentation PRs: create skeleton repo issue and initial stub for telemetry client (link above).
- Scheduler: sync with product (Console) to reserve a small dashboard slot for MVP metrics.

Appendix: quick checklist for SDK implementer (copy to PR template)
- Add non-blocking async telemetry client with env toggles.
- Emit sdk.first_request on first outbound call in session.
- Emit sdk.first_success/sdk.first_error with error_class and latency_ms.
- Ensure no request/response contents are captured.
- Implement sampling config via env var and an in-memory sampler.
- Add small integration test verifying events are emitted and attributes present.

This doc is intentionally lightweight and is meant to be a working spec that we can iterate on in PRs. Feedback requested on event set, sampling defaults, and rollout strategy.
